title: On‑call & Incident Response Playbook — Process, Runbooks, Postmortems, Rotations, Game Days, and Comms Templates
author: Jordan Patel
content:
Summary

This playbook documents Redwood Inference’s on‑call and incident response standards: incident lifecycle and severities, runbook structure and examples, postmortem expectations, on‑call rotation policy, game day guidance, and canonical status page / customer communications templates. It is intended for all engineers, SREs, and support staff who participate in alerts, mitigation, and customer communication.

Scope

- Services covered: Redwood API (hosted), Serving runtime, Dedicated control plane, Private deployment control plane, Observability & billing pipelines.
- Audiences: on‑call engineers, SREs, incident commanders, support/customer success, engineering managers, and SOC/security.

High‑level objectives

1. Reduce time‑to‑detection and time‑to‑mitigation while preserving safe operations.
2. Provide clear escalation paths and human roles for fast decisions.
3. Maintain consistent public and customer communication during incidents.
4. Produce actionable postmortems with measurable remediation and owners.

Incident severity & examples

- P0 (Sev 1): Total platform outage or data loss affecting production (e.g., all inference traffic returns 5xx, persistent data corruption). Target MTTR: 60 minutes. PagerDuty escalation window: immediate.
- P1 (Sev 2): Major functionality degraded for many customers (e.g., region‑wide latency spikes > 5x SLO, large backlog causing timeouts). Target MTTR: 4 hours.
- P2 (Sev 3): Partial degradation or single high‑impact customer incident (e.g., single model failing on requests for a major customer). Target MTTR: 24 hours.
- P3 (Operational): Non‑urgent operational issues, maintenance, or planned work.

Service Level Objectives (examples)

- Hosted API availability: 99.9% monthly.
- Inference token latency: p95 < 150ms for standard models (document model classes in model catalog).
- Error budget burn rate alert: > 5% of daily budget consumed in 1 hour triggers oncall review.

Roles & responsibilities

- Primary responder (Pager): Triage alerts, apply runbook steps, escalate if needed.
- Secondary responder: Backup for primary and takes over if primary needs support.
- Incident Commander (IC): Coordinates cross‑team activity for P0/P1; owns timeline and communications.
- Scribe: Records timeline, commands run, and decisions in the incident doc.
- Engineering Lead / Product Liaison: Approves customer communications for enterprise customers.

Escalation timeline (example)

1. Alert triggers PagerDuty to primary (0m). Primary ack within 5 minutes.
2. If no ack in 8 minutes or triage shows unresolved critical failure, escalate to secondary and on‑call manager.
3. For P0: IC assigned within 10 minutes. Incident channel and status page update posted within 30 minutes.

Alerting & tooling

- PagerDuty: primary oncall routing by service (hosting, runtime, infra, data).
- Slack: #incidents (read only for broad notices), dedicated private incident channel for the event (e.g., #incident-runtime-2026-03-04).
- Incident documentation: use the incident template in /confluence/eng-sre/incident-templates and link to the issue tracker ticket.
- Observability runbooks: Grafana dashboards, tracing, and logs links must be included in each service's runbook.

Runbook structure (required for every service)

Each service runbook must include the following flattenable sections (as plain text headings):

- Title and service owner (email, team).
- Detection: key metrics/alerts and thresholds.
- Immediate mitigation: steps to reduce customer impact (e.g., circuit breakers, scale up, fallback to model variant).
- Triage steps: commands, queries, dashboards, and expected outputs.
- Recovery & verification: smoke tests and success criteria.
- Rollback and post‑incident cleanup: config restores, cache invalidation.
- Postmortem checklist: data collection items and required graphs.
- Runbook test frequency: at least quarterly with game day or runbook smoke.

Example runbook: Inference service high latency / OOM\n
1) Detection
- Alerts that should trigger this runbook: inference_latency_p95 > 5x baseline for > 3 minutes OR instance OOM rate > 0.5% per minute.
- Dashboards: /grafana/dashboards/inference-latency, /grafana/dashboards/gpu-utilization.

2) Immediate mitigation (first 15 minutes)
- Step 1: Disable autoscaling cooldown extension: `redwoodctl patch autoscaler --service inference --cooldown 60s` (purpose: allow scale out).
- Step 2: Add capacity (if Dedicated): `terraform apply -var 'scale_add=2'` followed by coordinator workflow (ops approval required for production Dedicated).
- Step 3: Toggle degraded mode in API Gateway to serve cached prefetched responses for non‑critical routes: `api-gateway set-degraded --routes /health,/metrics`.
- Step 4: If OOMs persist, set model worker concurrency to 1: `kn apply -f scaledown-worker.yaml` then `restart deployment inference-worker`.

3) Triage (15–60 minutes)
- Check model KV cache hit rate: `curl -s https://metrics.internal/kvcache | jq .hit_rate` (expect > 80% normally).
- Inspect recent deployments: `git log -n 5 --pretty=oneline -- path/to/deployment` and `kubectl describe rs -n inference`.
- Check kernel/quantization changes in last 24 hours (link to model onboarding log).

4) Recovery & verification
- Run smoke test suite: `make smoke-test-inference` — all tests must pass with p95 < 2x baseline.
- Verify % 5xx errors reduced to baseline and latency p95 within SLO.

5) Rollback (if required)
- Revert last model or runtime change: follow the safe rollback checklist in the deployment ADR.
- Drain new nodes and redeploy previous stable revision.

6) Post‑incident cleanup
- Re-enable normal autoscaling and concurrency settings.
- Invalidate suspect cache entries.
- Open postmortem using the template below.

Postmortem template & expectations

All P0/P1 incidents must have a postmortem within 72 hours. Postmortems must be blameless, factual, and include measurable remediation. Required fields (document body text):

- Title (include incident ID and date).
- Severity (P0/P1/P2).
- Summary (one paragraph).
- Timeline (bullet list of timestamps and actions).
- Root cause analysis (technical and process).
- Immediate mitigations & long‑term remediation plan (with owners and due dates).
- Metrics: pre/post incident graphs (links), SLO burn rate, affected customer count.
- What went well / could be improved.
- Attachments: logs, runbooks used, PagerDuty alerts, Slack transcript export.

Postmortem approval & follow‑up

- Postmortem author assigns reviewers (must include SRE, owning service PM or ENG lead, and support).
- Reviewers have 3 business days to comment.
- IC or engineering manager closes with a postmortem status: Accepted / Needs more info.
- High‑impact remediation (prevent recurrence) must be tracked in Jira and linked from the postmortem; engineering manager verifies completion within the agreed timeline.

On‑call rotations and expectations

- Primary oncall rotation: 1 week (Mon 08:00 local → next Mon 08:00 local) by default for SREs and core infra teams.
- Secondary / buddy: Assigned per service; overlap one day for handoff.
- Handoffs: oncall engineer posts a handoff note in the weekly on‑call doc with known issues, ongoing alerts, and maintenance windows.
- Vacation / swap policy: swap via PagerDuty schedule UI and notify team Slack; swap must be approved by secondary.
- Pager hygiene: acknowledge alerts promptly; silence low‑priority noisy alerts after triage and open a ticket to fix flapping.

Game days & runbook validation

- Frequency: Quarterly game days per platform area (runtime, hosting, infra).
- Owners run scenarios that exercise detection, communication, mitigation, and postmortem creation.
- Required outcomes: runbook steps executed end‑to‑end, evidence of metric collection, status page update, and a short retrospective.

Status page & customer communications — templates

Guidelines
- Post public status updates within 30 minutes for P0 and P1 incidents.
- For enterprise customers, send a targeted email within 60 minutes after the incident is acknowledged and again on resolution.
- Keep public updates concise: current impact, affected regions/services, mitigation in progress, next update ETA.

Templates (copy/paste and edit)

1) Public status page initial update (short)\nTitle: Partial outage affecting Redwood API — investigating
Posted: {{timestamp}}
Impact: Some customers may experience increased latency and 5xx errors for text generation.
Scope: Hosted API (us‑west region).
Current status: We are investigating. Primary responders are actively triaging.
Next update: by {{timestamp + 30m}} or sooner.
Link: internal incident doc: {{link}}

2) Public status page follow‑up (mitigation in progress)\nTitle: Mitigation in progress for Redwood API latency incident
Posted: {{timestamp}}
Impact: Continued elevated latency for text‑generation endpoints in us‑west. ~40% of requests are served degraded (cached) responses.
What we changed: Added capacity and enabled degraded mode for non‑critical routes.
Next steps: Continue scaling and tracing root cause. Estimated next update in 1 hour.

3) Public status page resolved
Title: Incident resolved — Redwood API us‑west latency
Posted: {{timestamp}}
Impact: Elevated latency and 5xx errors resolved. Normal traffic restored.
What happened: Brief summary without sensitive internal details.
What we did: Capacity added, temporary degraded mode disabled, rollback of model runtime change.
Follow‑up: A postmortem will be published in 72 hours.

4) Enterprise customer notification (email) — initial
Subject: [Redwood] Incident affecting inference latency — we are investigating
Body:
Hello {{Customer Name}},

We are currently investigating an incident impacting inference latency for requests routed to us‑west. Our on‑call responders are triaging; we will follow up within 60 minutes with additional details and mitigation status.

Impact: Increased latency and intermittent 5xx errors for text generation.
Mitigation: Capacity added and degraded responses enabled for non‑critical routes.
Action requested: None at this time.

We apologize for the disruption. We will provide another update within 60 minutes or sooner.

Regards,
Redwood Inference Support

5) Enterprise customer notification — resolution
Subject: [Redwood] Incident resolved — inference latency (us‑west)
Body:
Hello {{Customer Name}},

The incident impacting inference latency in us‑west has been resolved at {{timestamp}}. Normal service has been restored and we are monitoring closely.

Summary: Root cause investigation is ongoing; we took immediate mitigations to restore service (capacity added, rollback of recent runtime change). A detailed postmortem will be shared within 72 hours.

If you experienced specific customer impact we have not addressed, please reply to this email and we will prioritize follow‑up.

Regards,
Redwood Inference Support

Incident documentation checklist (before closing)

- Incident timeline is complete and includes links to dashboards and logs.
- Runbook steps were followed and deviations documented.
- Postmortem created and reviewers assigned (P0/P1 only).
- Jira remediation ticket(s) created and linked.
- Customer communications sent and logged.

Appendix: Quick commands & links

- PagerDuty service pages: https://pagerduty.internal/services
- Incident template: /confluence/eng-sre/incident-templates
- Runbook index: /confluence/eng-platform/runbooks
- Grafana dashboards: /grafana/dashboards
- Smoke test: `make smoke-test-inference`

Revision history

- 2024-09-15: Created — Jordan Patel
- 2025-07-02: Added enterprise email templates and on‑call swap policy — Maya Lopez (reviewed)
- 2026-03-04: Updated escalation timeline and runbook example to include autoscaling controls — Jordan Patel

Notes and related policies

- This document is not a replacement for service‑specific runbooks; teams must maintain up‑to‑date runbooks under their service directories.
- For security incidents, follow Security IR procedures in security‑and‑compliance/incident-response-security.

End of playbook
